thread.title: Bulls And Bears: The Word That Says Why Bulls Will Win | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Bulls And Bears: The Word That Says Why Bulls Will Win | Investor's Business Daily
text:
U.S. stock indexes struggled in early trade Thursday, but the market turned mostly positive near midday. Meanwhile, bulls and bears trotted out their best arguments for and against the pressured uptrend.
X The Nasdaq added 0.5%, while the S&P 500 was just above flat. The Dow Jones industrial average trimmed its loss to 0.1%. Small caps moved into the positive neighborhood as the Russell 2000 inched up 0.3%.
Volume in the stock market faded on both major exchanges.
With the Nasdaq back to 12% off its high, the bears and the bulls alike have their reasons for their stances.
Bulls And Bears Bears can point to the chaos over Brexit in the United Kingdom and the fast drop in oil prices. The pessimists also can wheel out their best argument: The largely negative action of the stock market itself.
Bulls have a tougher argument. They can spotlight the put/call ratio's 1.21 reading at Wednesday's close. Readings at or above 1.2 suggest a short-term bottom is near. But that's a secondary indicator.
The optimists' best argument emerged with a report on the holdings of Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKA ).
Buffett and his team in the third quarter added shares in Apple ( AAPL ), Bank of America ( BAC ), Goldman Sachs ( GS ), U.S. Bancorp ( USB ), Bank of New York Mellon ( BK ), Delta Air Lines ( DAL ), General Motors ( GM ) and even financial technology provider StoneCo ( STNE ), a Brazilian stock.
Berkshire also opened a $4 billion position in JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ).
The One-Word Answer If conditions are so terrible, why is Buffett buying these stocks?
The answer might be summed up in one word: America. Many great stock market investors differ on their investing style, but they agree that betting against America is a bad idea.
Over the long haul, innovative products and new services have always emerged from America's openness to change.
Stocks On The Move Among IBD's 197 industry groups, computer networking stocks and chip designers scored some of the day's best gains.
In the networking space, Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) opened 6% higher and then gave back half the gain. Chip designer Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ) advanced 1.5% in the first 20 minutes of trade and then eased to a 0.8% gain.
After hours Wednesday, Cisco reported a 23% pop in fiscal Q1 earnings, the best growth in at least 20 quarters. Revenue rose 8%, also the best in at least 20 quarters. The Q1 quarter ended in October.
Analysts expect Cisco to grow earnings 15% in fiscal 2019 ending in July. The 15% annual growth would be the best in nine years.
Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ) is in the 5% buy zone from a Nov. 7 breakout in volume 362% above average.
On the downside, groups losing ground included department stores and data storage firms.
